To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

swimming training increased plasma levels and expression of ANP mRNA and reduced the expression of NPR-A and -C in kidney of hypertensive rats, while running training reduced expression of ANP only in the left atria.

the reduction in arterial pressure induced by exercise is dependent on training mode, as evidenced by a reduction in mean arterial pressure (P<0,05) and increased levels of ANF (P<0;05) in the swimming group, but not in the running group.
swimming but not running training reduces arterial pressure and increases ANP levels in SHR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of exercise training-induced blood pressure reduction in SHR, and the role of the natriuresis peptide system in this process.
the mechanisms by which swimming and running training affect the ANP system in SHR.
the mechanisms that may explain the reduction in arterial pressure induced by exercise training in SHR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
swimming training increases the plasma levels of ANF, and this increase is probably involved in the reduction in MAP.
swimming, but not running training, increased the ANP plasma levels and decreased the ANP mRNA expression in left atria and NPR-A and NPR- C expression in the kidney of SHR.
swimming, but not running training, increases the ANP plasma concentration and that this increase is involved in the reduction in blood pressure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
swimming and running training reduced MAP in SHR, and the mechanisms involved were different.
the MAP reduction in SHR is associated with a decrease in the expression of NPR-C in the kidney and with an increase in ANP in the plasma.
the MAP reduction observed after exercise is dependent upon the training modality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
swimming and running training reduced the MAP of SHR.
the reduction in arterial pressure induced by exercise training is modality-specific and is not associated with increased ANP levels in hypertensive rats.

the MAP reduction in SHR is dependent on the type of exercise, and that swimming training is associated with increased plasma ANP levels, which may be related to a reduction in the number of NPR-A and/or NPR-C in the kidney and mesenteric adipocytes.
